title: CTLS: Contrastive Tier-Based Lexical Selection Eliminates Temporal Dominance in Agent Memory Retrieval
research_question: Can a theoretically grounded tier-partitioned scoring rule that uses temporal decay only as a within-tier tiebreaker eliminate the temporal dominance failure mode and close the gap to BM25 without discarding temporal information entirely?

sections.title: Method

subsections.title: Frozen Memory and Matched Token Packing
subsections.goal: Full source histories are retained in a read-only single-layer bank, segmented losslessly into at most 256 pinned Qwen3 BPE tokens per turn segment. All selectors share the same source records, timestamps, metadata, memory wrapper, and whole-item first-fit overflow policy under 512, 1024, and 2048 tokens. BM25 (k1=1.2, b=0.75, positive IDF) and the existing hybrid (0.4 Jaccard + 0.3 temporal + 0.2 frequency + 0.1 importance) serve as baselines. The controlled bank is distinct from the legacy production Rail's 20-entry L1 capacity.

subsections.title: Contrastive Tier-Based Lexical Selection (CTLS)
subsections.goal: CTLS is a novel selector that partitions the candidate set into a lexically relevant tier (Jaccard overlap J(q,m) > 0) and a lexically absent tier (J(q,m) = 0) before applying any temporal scoring. Within the relevant tier, candidates are ranked by the full hybrid score so that temporal decay and frequency serve as tiebreakers among genuinely relevant items. Within the absent tier, recency-plus-importance ranks candidates for recency-based fallback. Final packing draws from the relevant tier first, then from the absent tier if budget remains. This partition provably satisfies a Non-Dominance Property: no zero-overlap item can outrank any positive-overlap item regardless of freshness gap or weight ratio, eliminating the temporal dominance condition identified in Equation (dom_condition). CTLS requires no model calls, no learned parameters, and no embedding model beyond the existing lexical tokenizer. It is a zero-cost selector substitution over the frozen candidate bank.

subsections.title: Repeated Real Agent Evaluation and Ablation Design
subsections.goal: The 84-question stratified LongMemEval-S subset spans six question types plus abstention, with three actual solver calls per question per selector per budget and isolated conversation IDs. Full 500-history retrieval is separate from QA. Real DeepAgents use qwen-plus-2025-12-01 at temperature zero with no tools and one iteration. The pinned official task-specific grading prompts use qwen3-max-2026-01-23 with a second fixed-model audit. The hybrid_no_time ablation (temporal weight set to zero, remaining weights renormalized) is the theoretically predicted upper bound for CTLS at queries with nonzero Jaccard overlap; their empirical gap on each budget measures the value of within-tier temporal tiebreaking. Eight synthetic banks each serve twenty distinct queries to measure write amortization.
